target_customer: Regulated bitcoin exchanges (as liquidity provider; Tinker earned from trading spreads)
problem: Early bitcoin exchanges had thin order books; an electronic market maker supplies liquidity and earns the spread.

founders.name: Gareth MacLeod
previous_startups: Fintech startup he grew to billions in transaction volume (named only on YC page as unnamed)

founders.name: Ross Robinson
founders.background_notes: Listed as software engineer; no background given

technical_complexity.rationale: Low-latency automated trading across immature exchange APIs with risk management; claimed peak of $10M+ daily volume (company claim).

defensibility.rationale: Market-making edge depends on strategy and speed that rivals can replicate; no structural moat found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents acting on this wedge; later professional market makers (B2C2 founded 2015, Cumberland desk 2014) entered the space.

market_need_then: Bitcoin exchanges in 2014 had limited liquidity; YC's own page claims Tinker represented 10-20% of BTCUSD volume on regulated exchanges at its peak (company claim, uncorroborated).

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B trading firm with no public brand footprint found.

outcome_analysis: Tinker reached a claimed 10-20% of BTCUSD volume on regulated exchanges and over $10M daily volume at its peak, then ceased operating, but no founder statement or press report on when or why was found, so the cause is not public. Candidate causes such as bitcoin's 2014-2015 bear market or thin spreads are unsourced and not recorded as factors.
notes: No dated direct market-making competitors were found in sources near 2014; list left empty (SFOX, a YC S14 exchange aggregator, appeared but is not a market maker). CB Insights lists investors YC, SV Angel, Tuesday Capital, FundersClub, Pegasus Tech Ventures with no amounts; unverified. Shutdown date and cause not public. Team size blank in directory.
